title: Requirements to production design
idea: A production design turns a short brief into scoped use cases, then into a domain model, tables, endpoints and screens that each trace back to a use case.

analogy.text: A restaurant plans its menu before building the kitchen. Each dish decides an appliance and a shelf; dishes left off the menu need no equipment.
analogy.breaks: A menu rarely changes; requirements change every release.

points: Write functional requirements as use cases: an actor, a verb, an outcome.
State scale and consistency needs as explicit assumptions, not as given facts.
List what is out of scope so nobody designs it by accident.
Trace every use case to an endpoint, a service method and a table.

items.label: Clarify
items.text: Ask who uses the system and what each actor must do. Write use cases.

items.label: Scope
items.text: Mark in and out. Assume scale, latency and which data must never be wrong.

items.label: Model
items.text: Nouns become entities and value objects; lifecycles become state machines in Java.

items.label: Store
items.text: Map the model to PostgreSQL tables; each invariant becomes a key or constraint.

items.label: Expose
items.text: Each use case becomes an endpoint with defined errors and safe retries.

items.label: Show
items.text: Screens follow the use cases. Each screen has loading, empty and error views.

code.title: Scope as code
code.caption: A clinic appointment system, the running example for this chapter. The scope lives in one enum you can review.

walk.text: Each in-scope use case names its actor, its endpoint and its main table.
Out-of-scope items stay listed with no endpoint, so the cut is visible and deliberate.
`inScope` is the rule: no endpoint means not built in this version.
Print the trace matrix: actor, use case, endpoint, table.
Scale is an assumption you state and size against, not a fact you were given.

pitfalls: Do not start with classes; agree on use cases and scope first.
Write numbers such as 500 doctors as assumptions, and say what changes beyond them.
Name the data that must stay correct under concurrency, such as one booking per slot.

quiz.q: Which use cases does UseCases print under Out of scope?
options: None: all six print in scope
quiz.why: `inScope` returns false when the endpoint is null. Only PAY_ONLINE and VIDEO_CALL were declared without an endpoint or a table.

takeaway: Every class, table and endpoint should trace back to a use case.

starters: Which questions should I ask the interviewer in the first five minutes?
How do I turn a non-functional requirement into a design decision?
How much capacity estimation does an LLD round expect?
